stem.text: A wire is bent into the shape of the graph of \( f(x) = 3 x e^{\frac{x}{4}} \) for \( 2 \le x \le 3 \), with x and y measured in meters. Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression in terms of x that gives the length of the wire.

worked_solution.text: By the product rule, \( f'(x) = \frac{3 \left(x + 4\right) e^{\frac{x}{4}}}{4} \).
The length is the integral of \( \sqrt{1 + \left(f'(x)\right)^{2}} \) over the interval: \( \int_{2}^{3} \sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{3 \left(x + 4\right) e^{\frac{x}{4}}}{4}\right)^{2}}\,dx \).

options.label: \( \int_{0}^{3} \sqrt{1 + \left(\frac{3 \left(x + 4\right) e^{\frac{x}{4}}}{4}\right)^{2}}\,dx \)
options.derivation: the lower limit taken as 0, the start of the axis, instead of the left end of the stated interval

options.label: \( \int_{2}^{3} \sqrt{1 + \frac{3 \left(x + 4\right) e^{\frac{x}{4}}}{4}}\,dx \)
options.derivation: the derivative left unsquared inside the radical

options.label: \( \int_{2}^{3} \left(1 + \left(\frac{3 \left(x + 4\right) e^{\frac{x}{4}}}{4}\right)^{2}\right)\,dx \)
options.derivation: the square root left off the arc length integrand
